title: Tech Note: Complex Invoice Printing Using Print Form
author: Thomas Maul, General Manager, 4D

historical_commentary.text: This note demonstrates advanced use of 4D 2004's enhanced Print Form command to produce a complex, multi-page invoice with distinct first-page/continuation headers and footers and automatic text wrapping of long item descriptions across page breaks, using a recompiled 1992-era LineStarts plug-in and a reusable PrintSmartForm method group. The specific plug-in and 4D Insider-based component-copying workflow are outdated, but the underlying Print Form layout technique (header/detail/break/footer zones) it teaches is conceptually still how 4D's classic form-based printing works today, making this a still-relevant pattern for anyone using 4D's traditional (non-4D Write Pro) printing approach.
related_updates: 4D Insider as a standalone tool has been integrated into or superseded by later 4D component/library management approaches
4D has since introduced 4D Write Pro (2016) as a more modern alternative for complex document generation, though classic Print Form remains supported
